html:
The Ashgabat earthquake struck the capital of Soviet Turkmenistan in the early hours of 6 October 1948. With a magnitude of 7.3, it destroyed most of Ashgabat in seconds and killed tens of thousands of people. Estimates range from about 10,000 to over 100,000.

Most victims died asleep when brick and mud buildings fell on them. Under Stalin, Soviet newspapers said little, and the true scale was kept secret for decades. Historians think the secrecy also kept the relief effort smaller than it should have been.

Among the dead were the mother and brothers of the boy Saparmurat Niyazov, who grew up in an orphanage and later ruled independent Turkmenistan as its president. He made the anniversary a day of national mourning. The city was rebuilt under Soviet rule in a new, planned form.
